title: A digitized book linked to its page regions (draft 0.3, 2026-11-06; 0.1 and 0.2 documents remain valid)
description: Four kinds of document share these definitions: a book's type list (format 'types'), one page's regions and units (format 'page'), a whole book assembled from its pages (format 'book'), and 0.3: a book's style sheet (format 'style'), how its types are printed. See schema/README.md. Rules that JSON Schema cannot express (references resolve, the units form a tree, types match) are checked by schema/book.py.

name.description: A type, flow or relation name.

unit_id.description: Page documents use local ids; a book document uses '<page id>#<local id>' of the unit's first fragment.

polygons.description: Outer rings in page-image pixel indices, largest piece first. Vertex (x, y) is the center of pixel column x and row y; in a corner-based system such as SVG, add 0.5 to both.

source.description: Provenance: which method, run, model or person produced this, and its raw evidence. Free-form.

style.description: 0.3: how something is printed, for renderings that resemble the book (a reader's 'as printed' view, HTML or typesetting exports). Presentation only: the units, their order and their text do not depend on it, and a semantic export may ignore it. Lengths are in points of the printed page. A unit's style overrides its type's in the book's style sheet; a line piece's overrides its unit's (on a line piece only font, size_pt, weight, italic and align apply; align sets the line apart, as a chapter's number and title).

font.description: A font role named in the style sheet's fonts, such as body, display or latin.

margin_left_pt.description: Left margin of every line, from the text block's (or the column's) left edge.

indent_pt.description: First line's indent from the others; negative where the first line hangs out (a numbered saying).

space_before_pt.description: Extra space above, beyond the normal line spacing.

row.description: Consecutive sibling units with the same row (on one page) are printed side by side, left to right in reading order, as the two columns of an address.

width.description: For a unit in a row: its share of the text width, from 0 to 1.

description.description: What a unit of this type is in this book. Used in prompts.

role.description: Furniture (running headers, page numbers, margin line numbers) belongs to the page, not to any unit.

region.description: The book-neutral region class (method 037's types). A type with a class is printed as regions; a type without one is a container only.

flow.description: If set, units of this type may stand at the top level of this flow.

lang.description: Default BCP 47 language tag, such as sa-Deva or en.

numbered.description: Units of this type usually carry a printed number.

formatting.description: How such spans are printed, if in one way.

start.description: Offset of the span's first character in the line piece's text (Unicode code points).

end.description: Offset just after its last character. A note marker is zero-width: start = end, at the position where the marker is printed.

kind.description: Generic formatting (bold, italic, small_caps, superscript, subscript, underline, spaced), note_marker, or one of the book's inline kinds.

id.description: Required for a note marker, which relations name; optional otherwise. Unique on the page.

marker.description: For a note marker, the marker as printed, such as १, 3 or *.

flows.description: Flow name to description. 'main' is the running text; others are, for example, 'notes'.

inline.description: 0.2: the book's own kinds of inline span, such as a pratīka, each with the generic formatting it is printed in.

line.description: The page-level line id from the line finder. Two regions sharing a printed line have pieces with the same id.

text.description: The transcription of this line piece, as printed (see the book's conventions).

end.description: How this piece joins the next piece of the same unit: a space; a printed hyphen to drop (the word continues); no space (the word continues without a hyphen); or a line break to keep, as between verse lines.

spans.description: 0.2: inline formatting and note markers over this piece's text, in order of start. Text formatted across a line break has a span on each piece.

style.description: 0.3: where this printed line differs from its unit (as a title page's lines in several sizes).

type.description: A type from the book's type list: the type of the unit that owns this region, or a furniture type.

polygons.description: Where local processing fails, the model's box as a rectangle, recorded in source.

box.description: 0.2: [x1, y1, x2, y2] in page pixels, the editable rectangle the outline is computed from (the region step's box, or the user's). The polygons and line pieces are derived from it and the page's ink.

order.description: Reading order on the page, as given by the region step. Evidence only: the book's order is the order of the units.

label.description: The printed page number in ASCII digits, if known.

children.description: In reading order: the unit's own regions (of its own type) and its child units.

number.description: The printed number or marker, such as 25 for a verse or 3 for a footnote.

style.description: 0.3: where this unit is printed differently from its type (centered, right-aligned, in a row with its neighbor).

open.description: In a page document, start means the unit began on an earlier page and end that it goes on on a later page. A book document keeps these flags only for units still open at the edges of the pages it includes.

anchor.description: 0.2: '<page id>#<span id>', the note-marker span the relation starts from. Preferred: it survives edits to the text.

start.description: Character offset in the line piece's text.

marker.description: The printed marker, such as 3 or *.

flows.description: Flow name to its top-level units, in reading order.

style_sheet.description: 0.3: how a book's types are printed: the defaults that units' and line pieces' own styles override.

text_box_pt.description: [x1, y1, x2, y2] of the text block on the page.

family.description: Font families in order of preference, as in CSS, ending with a generic family (serif, sans-serif).

description.description: What the book uses, such as the PDF's font names.
